mechanism_narrative: The observed week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last four weeks indicates a sustained recovery trend, which will continue to drive retail and recreation activity higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: As more people return to workplaces, indicated by WORKPLACES mobility rising above -50% from baseline, there will be a corresponding increase in incidental retail and recreation visits during commutes and lunch breaks, boosting RETAIL_REC.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -50% from baseline but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not increase relative to the prior 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility and increasing PARKS mobility suggests people are spending less time at home and more time outdoors. This increased general outdoor activity will spill over into nearby retail and recreation areas, driving RETAIL_REC up.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL continues to decrease while PARKS increases, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, increased public transit usage, as shown by rising TRANSIT mobility, indicates greater comfort with public spaces and a broader return to urban activity, directly supporting higher RETAIL_REC.
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility continues to rise, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days remains stagnant or declines.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility over the past four weeks indicates a sustained trend of people spending less time at home, which directly translates to more opportunities for out-of-home activities, including retail and recreation.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility continues its downward trend, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM mobility recovers to above -20% from baseline, it suggests a broader return to routine errands and local commerce, which will positively impact adjacent retail and recreation activities within a short horizon.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -20% from baseline but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days does not show an increase.

mechanism_narrative: As warmer weather encourages outdoor activities (PARKS increasing) and more people return to WORKPLACES, the combined effect of increased daytime foot traffic and leisure activities will boost RETAIL_REC, especially for businesses near parks or workplaces.
failure_condition: Both PARKS and WORKPLACES show an increasing trend, but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days decreases.

mechanism_narrative: In a continued reopening phase, if RETAIL_REC shows a consistent upward trend and TRANSIT mobility also increases, it indicates a broad societal return to pre-lockdown patterns, reinforcing the positive momentum for retail and recreation.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC and TRANSIT both show week-on-week increases for at least two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and TRANSIT both increase for two consecutive weeks, but the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the previous 28 days.
